svg.title: Qwen3.8-27B on one Tesla V100 32 GB
svg.desc: Qwen3.8-27B decode and prefill on one Tesla V100: ashalliants/ninfer-3090 with DFlash2 K7 and with MTP3 against Lapilli.
svg.text: Qwen3.8-27B on one Tesla V100 32 GB
ashalliants/ninfer-3090 against Lapilli (chris83-dev/lapilli-v100 f9b7dd09), both run on this card with the same
prompts, greedy, 300 output tokens, warm. Both of our configurations are shown: each wins different prompts.
Conversation (temperature 0.6) and JSON are Lapilli's basalt-bench fixtures (seed 7); the JSON prompt runs to about 7.2-7.6K output

path.title: Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): story 61.5 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): code 147 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): Chinese 41.4 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): French 69.0 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): thinking 116.5 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): conversation 103.5 tok/s
Ours, DFlash2 K7 + n-gram 15 (router): JSON 190 tok/s

svg.text: tokens per second, higher is better
A fresh prompt each time, two repeats each (ours 951-958 at 4.2K).
tokens per second, higher is better
Decode after a prompt of that many tokens, build 3c6a616d with #608/#609, against master before them. Lapilli was not run at long
tokens per second, higher is better
Where we lose: our DFlash2 router configuration is slower than Lapilli on story (61.5 vs 69.0) and Chinese (41.4 vs 48.3); MTP3 wins
those but is slower than Lapilli on code (110.2 vs 119.9) and JSON (126.1 vs 175.8). Use MTP3 for prose and non-English text, DFlash2
for code, thinking and structured output.
Quants differ: ours is the Qwen3.8-27B Q4/Q5 group-quant mix (19.0 GB), Lapilli runs its Qwen3.8-27B QUASAR NVFP4 pack (21.1 GB). A
second Lapilli run agreed: story 69.3, code 123.0, thinking 97.2.
One Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB on a PCIe Gen3 x4 eGPU link, 59 GiB host RAM · 200 W limit · 2026-11-25 · ours: build d309f3d8 (long context:
3c6a616d, #608/#609) · competitors measured on this box unless marked “reported”
